title: Maximum Score From Removing Stones
summary: In a solitaire game with three piles of stones, each turn involves removing one stone from two different piles to earn a point.
statement: In a solitaire game with three piles of stones, each turn involves removing one stone from two different piles to earn a point. The game concludes when fewer than two piles remain non-empty. Given the initial sizes of the piles, calculate the maximum score achievable.
constraints: Each move removes one stone from each of two different nonempty piles and earns one point.
hints: The score cannot exceed half the total stones or the number outside the largest pile.
These two upper bounds are both achievable by repeatedly pairing the largest available piles.
If one pile dominates, every move consumes one outside stone; otherwise stones can be paired until fewer than two remain.
editorial: If one pile dominates, every move consumes one outside stone; otherwise stones can be paired until fewer than two remain.

tests.explanation: The two smaller piles contain six stones total, allowing six moves against the largest pile.
Seven pairs can be removed before fewer than two piles remain nonempty.
